To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a versatile aldol strategy that enabled us to synthesize callipeltosides A and B and aurisides, and that we have revised the stereochemical assignment of the marine polyketide dolostatin 19.

the total synthesis of a novel family of structurally related 14-membered glycosidic macrolides of diverse biological activity was accomplished by a convergent aldol-based approach, and that the total synthesis and stereochemical assignment of the cytotoxic dolastatin 15 was completed.
a novel class of 14-membered marine macrolides can be synthesized in a concise manner using an efficient aldol-based strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the total syntheses and stereochemical revisions of four marine macrolides, callipeltosides A, B, and C and dolastatins 15, 19, and 20.
the total synthesis of a novel class of glycosidic macrolides of natural product origin.
the development of a new class of glycosidic macrolides of biological interest, and the application of novel strategies and methods to the total synthesis of structurally complex natural products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these studies represent the first examples of a total synthesis of a marine macrolide that incorporates a glycosidic linkage.
the synthesis of these natural products, and the associated studies, have led to a deeper understanding of the biosynthesis of these complex natural products.
the total syntheses described in this thesis have led to the discovery of a new family of marine natural products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a novel synthetic strategy was developed that enabled us to access the first examples of structurally related macrolides of natural origin, callipeltosides A and B.
the aldol reaction is a powerful synthetic tool for the preparation of a variety of complex molecules.
the aldol-based synthetic strategy has been successfully applied to a variety of structurally related polyketide targets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a judicious combination of biogenetically inspired synthetic planning and conformational considerations can lead to the efficient synthesis of complex natural products and related compounds.
the stereochemical assignment for dolastatin 9, a structurally similar polyketide isolated from the same organism, was erroneous and that dolastatin 10 is the correct structure for this compound.

the aldol strategy can be used to access a wide range of polyketide structures, including those that contain multiple stereogenic centers and are highly oxygenated, by judicious choice of the aldol donor and aldol acceptor.
